summary: Pulled the matched extra-EU Chapter 72 export series (1999-2025, all 27 years, value and mass) from live Comext DS-045409 (vintage 2026-10-16), re-pulled imports (26 of 27 years reproduce the workbook table; only 2023 differs, by -0.45 EUR m and -0.22 kt), and built the X-M balance, the materiality shares and the by-product series. Extra-EU Ch72 balance is positive in every year 1999-2025 (+3,218 kt and +EUR 3,837 m in 2025), but exports are at a 27-year low in tonnes (4,681 kt) and the surplus widened only because imports fell faster (-68% vs -35%, 2017-2025). The extra-EU series is small: 6.1% of German Ch72 import tonnes in 2025 (13.4% in 2017) and 16.0% of export tonnes, so S7's "roughly a tenth" should become about 8% (2024) or 6% (2025). An unrequested finding: heading 7203 (direct-reduced iron) explains 31% of the 2017-2025 fall in extra-EU imports and 84% of the 2025 fall. No classification break at heading level for any series used; HS 2007 split sub-headings of 7304 and 7306 only.

key_facts.label: Extra-EU Ch72 exports, selected years (EUR m / kt)
Import re-pull vs workbook update-tab 4.2
key_facts.value: 26 of 27 years match after 2-dp rounding. Only 2023 differs: value 2,106.93 vs 2,107.38 EUR m (-0.45, -0.02%); mass 2,088.77 vs 2,088.99 kt (-0.22, -0.01%). key_facts.label: Materiality: extra-EU share of German Ch72 trade (mass / value)
Extra-EU share of the 2017-2025 change in all-partner Ch72 trade
key_facts.value: All-partner imports fell 10,368 kt (34,425 to 24,057); extra-EU accounts for 3,160 kt = 30.5% while holding 13.4% of 2017 tonnage. All-partner exports fell 4,316 kt; extra-EU accounts for 2,536 kt = 58.8%.

key_facts.label: Comext Ch72 all-partner balance vs workbook Dataset B
key_facts.value: Comext Ch72 WORLD X-M (Mt): -0.9 (2017), -0.5, +2.2, +4.5, +1.4, +2.1, +5.2, +5.2 (2024). Dataset B (steel mill products, rounded): -1.2, -1.6, +0.3, +1.4, -0.4, +0.4, +3.0, +4.1. Same direction, different levels, sign differs in 2021 (+1.4 vs -0.4). In 2017 the extra-EU balance was +2.6 Mt while intra-EU was -3.5 Mt and all-partner -0.9 Mt.

key_facts.label: Heading 7203 (direct-reduced / spongy iron) drives the Ch72 import fall
key_facts.value: Extra-EU imports 1,016 kt (22% of Ch72 import tonnes) in 2017, 438 kt in 2024, 28 kt in 2025. Share of fall: 987 kt = 31% of 2017-2025 fall (3,160 kt); 667 kt = 36% of 2021-2025 fall (1,874 kt); 410 of 491 kt = 84% of the 2024-2025 fall. 7204+7207+7208 together explain only 720 kt (23%) of the 2017-2025 fall. Cause not established.

key_facts.label: Scrap 7204 and other by-product imports (extra-EU, kt)
key_facts.value: 7204 scrap imports 705.6 (2017) to 393.9 (2025), 26.9% of Ch72 import tonnes in 2025; scrap exports to non-EU 1,230.8 kt in 2025 (net exporter +837 kt), unit value 452 EUR/t imports. 7207: 1,104.0 (2008) to 175.2 (2025). 7208: 733.6 (1999) to 32.7 (2025). 7304: 87.4 kt / EUR 233.3 m (2025). 7306: 159.4 kt / EUR 232.4 m. 26011200 agglomerated ore: 7,165.7 (2018 peak), 4,902.0 (2024), 2,035.1 kt (2025, -58%), 117 EUR/t. 26011200 exports return only 5 years, EUR 635 to 93,871 a year.

key_facts.label: Why imports rose after 2005 and the 2022 unit-value jump
key_facts.value: 2004 to 2005 extra-EU imports +838 kt, of which 7207 semi-finished +714 kt (85%); 2004 to 2007 +2,384 kt, 7207 +769 kt (32%). 2021 to 2022 unit values rose inside headings too: 7203 +32%, 7204 +21%, 7207 +12%, 7208 +45% (aggregate 828 to 1,176 EUR/t); unit values are mix-affected, not price indices.

key_facts.label: Classification breaks
key_facts.value: WCO Table I for HS 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022 lists no entries for 7204, 7207, 7208 or 2601.12; HS 2007 subdivided subheadings inside 7304 and 7306 (and merged subheadings inside 7225/7226/7229). Live data agree: HS6 code sets under 7204, 7207, 7208 identical in all years 1999-2025; 7304/7306 HS6 codes split in 2007. 7304XX (not elsewhere specified/confidential) is used 1999-2005 only and holds 6-14% of 7304 export value; heading totals include it. EXT/INT aggregates are fixed 2020 composition (UK extra-EU throughout). No break at heading level for the series used.

key_facts.label: Comext partner and revision concepts (ESMS)
key_facts.value: Extra-EU imports are assigned by country of origin, intra-EU imports by country of consignment; statistical value is CIF imports / FOB exports; CN is revised yearly; detailed data considered final by October of the following reference year.

caveats: Single vintage (Comext updated 2026-10-16); Eurostat revises monthly and says data are final by October of the following year, so 2025 (and possibly 2024) can still move. Re-run pull_comext.py after the next update; the next update date was not found.
The cause of the 2023 and 2025 differences versus the workbook is not verified; the earlier vintage cannot be retrieved from the dissemination API.

Values are nominal EUR (CIF imports, FOB exports); no deflation. Chapter 72 includes scrap, pig iron, ferro-alloys, DRI and semi-finished goods and excludes Chapter 73 products and ore: not the CBAM base. Whether CBAM covers each heading (for example 7203) was not checked.

Direct trade only: extra-EU imports are assigned by country of origin and intra-EU by country of consignment, so non-EU steel cleared in another member state is invisible here; EXT/INT aggregates use the fixed 2020 EU27 composition (UK extra-EU throughout) and exist only from 1999.
A positive extra-EU balance is not a competitiveness verdict and is not national-accounts NX: imports fell much faster than exports and export tonnes are at a 27-year low.
Causes of the 7203 collapse, the 2025 halving of agglomerated ore imports and the 2005 jump in 7207 are not established by this data.

Classification findings rest on my reading of WCO Table I PDFs (extracted text, guide with no legal status) plus live HS6/CN8 data; heading-level moves between chapters were only checked through the entries found.
